models.summary: Health is one closeness score from 23 indicators under five headings: resource, environment, connect, achievement, sustainable. Each indicator is bent into [0,1] by a method suited to its shape: logistic for unbounded ones, max or min scaling, a moderate form, and a Cauchy membership for graded judgments. Weights mix AHP, entropy and the coefficient of variation. TOPSIS gives the score. Fuzzy clustering of 40 countries draws the bands: above 0.5 super healthy, 0.36 to 0.5 sub-healthy, below 0.22 unhealthy. Italy scores 0.31 and ranks 26th.

objectives: Score any country on a common scale and grade it.

details: 40 countries across continents and income levels. Five headings, 23 indicators.
Cauchy membership fixed by three points: grade 1 maps to 0.01, grade 3 to 0.8, grade 5 to 1.

parameter_estimation.method: AHP for one set of weights, entropy for the inferior indicators, coefficient of variation for the five headings, then a combination. The combination rule is not printed. The judgment matrix is omitted for space.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not applicable. Consistency check for AHP mentioned, ratio not given.

details: Italy 0.31, rank 26 of 40. Bands at 0.5, 0.36 and 0.22. The vision score is 0.41823.

constraints: Larger always means better after transformation.
strengths: The normalization is chosen per indicator, with the reason stated for the logistic.
Three weighting methods are combined precisely because each errs differently.
limitations: Indicator choice is later conceded to be subjective.
assumptions: Countries within 0.03 of income are comparable.

models.summary: Income enters as INNI. Twenty-one of twenty-three indicators rise with it; graduate debt and the cost index do not. An exponential curve of NHHE on INNI fits best and becomes the expected score. A country above the curve is healthier than its income predicts. Italy, furthest below, drops from 26th to last. The UK, inside the band 0.77 to 0.83 around Italy's 0.80, scores far higher and becomes the benchmark. Holt smoothing, R-squared 0.6367 and 0.6393, forecasts UK income from 0.81296 to 0.83129. Prose sets Italy at 95 percent of the UK overall, resource 95, environment 95, connect 90, achievement 95, sustainable 100. The printed vision is 0.41823, 0.47360, 0.71868, 0.69189, 0.28799, 0.47369. Against UK figures 0.44, 0.49853, 0.75650, 0.76877, 0.28799, 0.49862, the first four match the stated shares, but achievement prints the UK value itself (100 percent, not 95) and sustainable prints 95 percent of the UK (not 100). Italy then crosses the curve.

details: INNI for 2019 across 40 countries. Italy at 0.80. UK income series 1995 to 2019.
Comparability band of plus or minus 0.03. Vision capped below the UK: 95 percent overall, 90 for connect, 100 for sustainable.
Cross-section plus a fifteen-year forecast, no equilibrium.

parameter_estimation.method: Linear and quadratic regressions per indicator, then several curves for the score, exponential kept. Four smoothers compared; Holt kept on R-squared of 0.6367 and 0.6393.

algorithm.description: Fit the curve, measure vertical gaps, pick the worst gap, find a peer in the income band, forecast the peer, scale the target down from it.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Best fit among the forms tried. No residual is printed.

details: Italy falls from 26th, score 0.31, to 40th. UK income 0.81296 rising to 0.83129. UK forecast NHHE 0.44, resource 0.49853, environment 0.75650, connect 0.76877, achievement 0.28799, sustainable 0.49862. Italy vision 0.41823, 0.47360, 0.71868, 0.69189, 0.28799, 0.47369.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The re-ranking is the result. A country mid-table in absolute terms is last in relative terms, which is the reason it is chosen. Four vision numbers match the stated shares of the UK. Achievement does not: prose says 95 percent, the cell equals the UK figure. Sustainable does not either: prose says 100 percent, the cell is 95 percent of 0.49862.

constraints: Vision set below the peer, not equal to it.
strengths: The benchmark is a real country at a similar income, not an invented optimum.
The target is discounted below the benchmark, and the discount differs by component.
limitations: The no-policy path uses predicted income rather than recomputed history, which the authors flag.
The fitted coefficients are not printed.
missing_details: The other countries inside the 0.77-0.83 band.
assumptions: Income and health move together except for debt and cost.

models.summary: ANOVA on 10 percent and 20 percent lifts isolates five indicators: education spending share, policy freedom, share of international teachers, number of top-1000 universities, and the stock of full-time researchers. Policy runs in three five-year stages from 2021 to 2035. A system dynamics model links the five interventions to the indicators and to the score. Spending is assumed to rise from 1.5 percent of GDP to 2 percent. The simulated score rises and steepens. Moving spending by half a point of GDP does not change the direction.
models.purpose: Show the phased policy reaches the vision, and that the path is not an artifact of the spending assumption.
objectives: Trace fifteen years of policy into a path for the health score.

variables.definition: Annual policy intensity, quantified and fed into the model
Higher-education spending as a share of GDP, from 1.5 toward 2

details: Italy, 2021. Spending at 1.5 percent of GDP.
Three stages, 2021-2025, 2026-2030, 2031-2035. Spending raised to 2 percent.
The path is still rising at 2035. No steady state is stated.

parameter_estimation.method: Rates are not estimated in the text. The five indicators were chosen by ANOVA, not fitted here.

algorithm.description: Quantify each year's policy, run the stock-and-flow model, read the score.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: None stated. The path is accepted because it rises and steepens.

details: The score rises across fifteen years and the slope increases from stage to stage. A shift of 0.5 percent of GDP leaves the direction unchanged.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The shape of the path is the evidence. Without rates, the level reached in 2035 cannot be verified, only the claim that it hits the vision.

constraints: Spending capped at 2 percent of GDP.
strengths: The levers are chosen by a test rather than by taste.
The same model is then disturbed to see whether the direction survives.
limitations: No equation, no parameter, no fit statistic.
Effectiveness is inferred from a curve the model itself drew.
assumptions: Correlated indicators move with the five chosen ones.
